disease_label_per_paper: Pleural empyema in a patient with a perinephric abscess and diaphragmatic defect

past_history: advanced multiple sclerosis complicated by quadriplegia

presentation_summary: 68-year-old nursing home resident with advanced multiple sclerosis, quadriplegia, cognitive impairment, bedbound status, incontinence, chronic indwelling urinary catheter, recurrent UTIs, and remote right pyelonephritis presented with 1 week of fever and increasing dyspnea.
On presentation she was febrile to 39 C, tachycardic at 130/min, normotensive, and in respiratory distress.
Clinical examination showed signs of a large right pleural effusion without abdominal tenderness.
Labs showed marked leukocytosis 68 x10^9/L and CRP 500 mg/L.
CT thorax showed extensive peribronchial thickening, right lower-lobe consolidation, and a complex right pleural effusion with thickened pleura.

Initial treatment was IV piperacillin-tazobactam and urgent 12F intercostal catheter drainage; subsequent pleural and retroperitoneal cultures grew Morganella morganii, and CT abdomen showed a right perinephric/psoas collection extending into the thoracic cavity through a likely pre-existing posterolateral diaphragmatic defect.

outcome_follow_up.description: After pleural drainage, meropenem, intrapleural tPA/DNase, and CT-guided drainage of the perinephric/psoas abscess, she had sustained defervescence and normalization of inflammatory markers. She was discharged to residential care with four further weeks of IV antibiotics and remained well.

quality_warnings: Pleural pH, pleural culture, retroperitoneal pus culture, diaphragmatic-defect review, tPA/DNase response, and outcome are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Ranking evidence keeps the initial respiratory presentation, vitals, exam, blood inflammation, CT thorax, and source-context risk without using final culture or drainage proof.
The abdominal source is preserved because pleural empyema can arise from extrapulmonary contiguous infection; it should not be deleted to force a purely pneumonic pattern.
